title: Unified Signalboard and Lifecycle Automation for Cross-Team Roadmap Dependencies
creator: Leo Martinez
description:
Problem: We frequently see blockers during canary/A-B rollouts because cross-team dependencies (infra, security, design, serving runtime) are not captured or monitored consistently. Current ad-hoc tracking (spreadsheets + Slack threads) misses lifecycle state and ownership, which inflates lead time and increases risk for high-value releases.

Goal: Build a lightweight "Signalboard" that provides a single pane showing roadmap items (features/initiatives) + explicit dependency edges, lifecycle status (identified, acknowledged, in-flight, mitigated), risk score, and automated escalation/remediation steps. The Signalboard will be backed by Linear and syncs with GitHub PR status and a simple webhook from the Console rollout API.

Non-goals: Not building a full dependency resolver or replacing Linear as the canonical ticket system. Not implementing heavy graph DB in Phase 1.

Approach summary: Phase 1 (MVP) = read-only Signalboard view in Console + nightly sync from Linear labels and a webhook to pull PR/build statuses. Provide per-dependency owner, due date, and an autogenerated risk score (calculated from priority, ETA proximity, and blocked status). Add flows to create follow-up tasks in Linear with a single click. Phase 2 = two-way sync + lifecycle automation (automatic status transitions, SLA timers, escalations).
acceptance_criteria: Signalboard UI shows all P0/P1 roadmap items for current cycle with listed dependencies and owners
Nightly sync from Linear imports dependency edges and maps owners for >=90% of items without manual editing
Risk score and SLA timer are visible on each dependency and update within 10 minutes of webhook events
Action button creates a pre-filled Linear follow-up ticket with link back to the Signalboard
Pilot completed with infra and serving-runtime teams and documented feedback session recorded
rollout_plan: Week 0 (Discovery): Interview 6 PMs + 4 Eng leads + 2 Security reps to validate signals and escalation needs
Sprint 1 (MVP): Implement nightly Linear sync + basic Signalboard UI (read-only) and risk heuristic
Sprint 2 (Pilot): Enable one-click follow-up creation and webhook integration to GitHub/Console for live status
Pilot Duration: 4 weeks with infra & serving-runtime; collect metrics and iterate
Post-pilot: Expand to Design and Security, iterate on 2-way sync and SLA automation
metrics_and_success: Reduce rollout-blocked rate for P0/P1 by 50% vs baseline (baseline = 18%)
Median time to resolve a cross-team dependency < 5 days during pilot
Coverage: >=95% of roadmap items with documented dependencies for next release window
Adoption: 8/10 PMs in pilot report Signalboard as "helpful" in post-pilot survey
risks_and_tradeoffs: Trade-off: Read-only MVP avoids complex two-way sync implementation but needs manual correction flows
Risk: Owners may not keep dependency metadata updated — mitigated via periodic reminders and lightweight follow-up ticket creation
Risk: Security concerns about exposing CI/build statuses in Console — we will only surface pass/fail and link to internal GH checks, not tokens or logs
Trade-off: Using Linear labels + webhook as canonical ingest avoids building a new datastore but may require mapping logic for custom workflows
open_questions: What is the minimum viable data model for a dependency edge? (fields: owner, due_date, type, impact) — propose starting with owner/due_date/type
Should risk score weight proximity to release higher than priority? (proposal: 60% proximity, 30% priority, 10% historical block rate)
Who owns SLA enforcement and escalation — Product or Program Ops? Recommend Program Ops for initial run
Do we require explicit opt-in for projects outside Redwood core repos? (proposal: opt-in for third-party integrations)
